combat_wing: 41st CBW (flew as High group of the 41st CBW per 303-01)
dispatched_notes: 303-01 header: 'Crews Dispatched: 20' and 'the 303rd BG(H) dispatched 20 crews and 204 men'; the same document's 1st Air Division table shows 303BG (19). 2 aborted (Campbell 42-29524, Brown 42-5257). Lost = 1 MIA over Germany (Sanders, 42-29477); in addition 42-5482 was abandoned over England and crashed at Risley (crew safe), so 2 aircraft destroyed in total. 303-01 also says one aircraft was written off after landing and fifteen damaged.

aircraft.loss_details: Shot down about five minutes after leaving the target; seen hit by a rocket from an Me 210 which knocked off the elevator and rudder; went down on fire between Nos. 3 and 4 engines and crashed near Bamberg, Germany. 2 KIA (Carll, Cockrum), 9 POW (303-01, 303-04, 303-05).
aircraft.notes: 11 men aboard. Crew photo captions name 2Lt F.M. Peacock as navigator, but 303-01/303-04 state Peacock was not aboard and 2Lt Gordon W. Wood flew as navigator. 303-05 lists only 10 (omits Martin) and spells co-pilot 'Henry C. Nogash'. Previously 42-29477 'Little Audrey' with 306th BG 369th BS (WW-H), transferred to 303rd 25 Sep 1943 (303-05). Carll and Cockrum buried Lorraine American Cemetery (303-01). Kremer later repatriated (303-04).

aircraft.formation_position: Assembly chart (303-01 p.10): left-hand squadron, second row, inner position
aircraft.loss_details: Not a combat loss over enemy territory: abandoned in mid-air over England on return (fog at Molesworth, almost out of fuel, rudder controls shot away). Crashed at Risley, about ten miles south of Molesworth. All ten crew bailed out safely.
aircraft.notes: Badly damaged (rudder controls shot away, radio compass and instruments out), nearly out of fuel; base fogged in, crew ordered to bail out over England. All ten bailed out safely (Caterpillar Club); aircraft crashed at Risley in the back yard of 170 High Street (303-01). Kujawa appears as 'Anthony T. Kujawa' in the 303-01 claims list (ME-110 destroyed). Index (303-03) records C/L 14 Oct 43 Risley.

research_gaps: Service numbers: none recorded; 303-01 does not give them. MACR 907 (Sanders) would list them for the lost crew - not retrieved (americanairmuseum.com returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool; NARA/Fold3 MACR not accessed).
MACR number 907 for 42-29477 is from one secondary source (303-05) only; needs checking against the MACR index.
Block numbers for 19 of 20 aircraft not researched/recorded (only 42-29477 = B-17F-55-BO, PROBABLE). Could be filled from Joe Baugher's serial lists.
Individual wounded: 303-01 says five arriving crewmen were wounded; only Sgt James R. Teno (41-24619) is named. Other returning crew are marked 'returned' with fate_confidence PROBABLE.

Which aircraft was 'written off after landing' (303-01) is not stated; 42-5482 (crashed at Risley after bail-out) is recorded as written_off. 15 aircraft damaged, but only 42-5393, 42-5081, 41-24619, 42-3158 have documented damage.
Whether each non-aborting aircraft actually bombed the primary is assumed from 303-01 (no other early returns listed); 42-5393 salvoed its bombs before the target per pilot Heller.
Formation: the 303-01 assembly chart labels no squadrons (lead/high/low); positions are recorded as drawn. Klint's account mirrors left/right versus the chart for Hullar and Ness.
Aircraft letters come from the 303-03 index read through a summarising fetch; not individually confirmed on aircraft pages except VK-B, GN-Y, GN-I.
